data.hypothesis: The valid flattened-tile 32x64x64 scalar 4x4 candidate measured 0.033899 s mean, while the valid row-band and B-packed variants measured 0.035286 s and 0.072814 s. This experiment changes only the output row block to 64 while retaining the 4x4 register microkernel, 64-column/reduction blocks, first-reduction overwrite, and static tile ownership. A larger row tile may reuse each B panel across more output rows and reduce tile scheduling work; its larger footprint may instead hurt locality. The candidate is unmeasured.
data.notes: This is a controlled 32-to-64 row-block contrast against the prior flattened-tile design; it adds no packing or target-specific ISA mechanism. Prior measured T3 results: flattened-tile parallel 0.0338991503 s, row-band 0.0352859577 s, and B-packed 0.0728142878 s; all were reported valid. These do not establish the reason for their timings. The controller must validate all official sizes and collect repeated native n=1024 timings; no performance or correctness result is claimed for this candidate.
transformations: Replace the size-specialized reference traversal with a generic blocked GEMM using 64x64 output tiles and 64-element reduction blocks, with bounds-safe edge handling.
Use a scalar unrolled 4x4 output microkernel with sixteen local accumulators; initialize accumulators to zero on the first reduction block and load prior C values only on subsequent blocks.
Assign independent flattened output tiles to a static OpenMP loop, capping worker count by the caller's thread budget and tile count; retain serial behavior without OpenMP.
Do not pack operands or add explicit SIMD or ISA-specific code, isolating the row-block-size change.
